agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration / NASA Ames Research Center
payload: Outer-system flyby spacecraft; SNAP-19 RTGs (~165 W at launch); twin of Pioneer 10
credit: © NASA / Ames Research Center — U.S. Government work, public domain. First spacecraft to fly past Saturn (1979-09-01) and the first to image the planet at close range. Used Jupiter's gravity to reach Saturn, demonstrating the gravity-assist technique that would later send Voyager 2 to Uranus and Neptune. Discovered Saturn's F ring + a small inner moon (later resolved by the Voyagers into the co-orbital pair Janus/Epimetheus). Carries the same Pioneer plaque as Pioneer 10. Signal lost 1995-09-30 from a heliocentric distance of ~43 AU; spacecraft heading toward the constellation Aquila.

events.label: Launch — Atlas / Centaur
events.description: Cape Canaveral, 1973-04-06. Launched after Pioneer 10's successful Jupiter encounter — Pioneer 11's primary purpose was to use Jupiter's gravity to reach Saturn ahead of the Voyagers and scout the ring-plane crossing geometry.

events.label: Jupiter — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 42,800 km above the cloud tops on 1974-12-02 — even closer than Pioneer 10. Returns the first images of Jupiter's polar regions and confirms the magnetosphere boundary's response to the solar wind. The flyby bends the trajectory dramatically — slingshot raises the aphelion past Saturn at a high inclination.

events.label: Saturn — flyby
events.description: Closest approach 20,900 km above Saturn's cloud tops on 1979-09-01 — the first spacecraft to visit Saturn, two years ahead of Voyager 1. Discovered the thin F-ring and a small inner moon (later resolved by the Voyagers into the co-orbital pair Janus/Epimetheus); the ring-plane crossing geometry it tested cleared the Voyagers to attempt the same path. Last contact 1995-09-30.
